title: Planning maps are for adults
statement: Treat a curriculum planning map as a guide for adults: never copy its rows into student material without separate review, or take a row as proof of learning.
example: All 189 review-comment cells in one draft ledger are blank, which records no comments, not approval.
detail: The routing packet for review feedback on the reading course says to treat the draft science workbook's rows as a candidate adult-facing coherence map, not approved student wording or proof that a student has already learned a concept (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/README.md`). Draft ledgers for several grades carry the same boundary: one is not evidence that younger students learned its concepts, another warns never to assume its concepts were taught, mastered, reviewed or approved, and a third forbids turning its statements into student prose without a separate authoring and review process (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0152-science-g8-atom-composite-ledger.qmd`, `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0149-draft-grade-5-science-ledger.qmd`, `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0150-science-g6-atom-composite-ledger.qmd`). The passage-integrity checks forbid copying a draft workbook sentence into child-facing prose without separate review, and the cross-subject guidance notes that the draft science standards are written for adults and do not reflect the language students will be given (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/science-passage-agent.md`, `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0137-science-social-studies-reencounter-guidance.qmd`). Rows copied into student material need separate authoring as well as review, and a row is no proof that a student was even taught it.
